string.doc: Accepts a JSON string. Null or an absent value gives required; any other kind gives type_mismatch with expected "string".

int.doc: Accepts a JSON number written as an integer (no fraction, no exponent) within the int32 range. Null or absent gives required; another kind, or a number with a fraction or an exponent, gives type_mismatch with expected "integer"; an integer outside the range gives type_mismatch.numeric_range.

long.doc: As int, within the int64 range, with expected "long".

float.doc: Accepts any JSON number and rounds it to the nearest float32; a number whose magnitude rounds beyond the float32 range gives type_mismatch.numeric_range; both type mismatches have expected "float". A number with a minus sign whose value is zero gives -0, whatever its form: -0, -0.0, -0e0 and -0.000e10 alike, and so does a negative number that rounds to zero.

double.doc: As float, with float64 and expected "double".

decimal.doc: Accepts any JSON number, keeping the scale its lexeme gives. Another kind gives type_mismatch with expected "number".

list.doc: Accepts a JSON array and decodes each element with the element decoder at the path of its index. The issues of every failing element are given, in index order.

dict.doc: Accepts a JSON object and decodes each member's value with the value decoder at the path of its name.

object.doc: Decodes each field from the same input, in the order the fields are declared, and gives the product of their values. Each field checks for itself that the input is an object: a required field of a non-object input gives type_mismatch (expected "object") at the field's path, and an optional field reads a non-object input as not having the field. The issues of every failing field are given, in declaration order.

strictObject.doc: As object, and in addition gives unknown_field, at the member's path, for every member of an object input that no field names, in the order of the input's members. Every field names its member: a flat field, which reads the whole input, would leave the members it reads unknown.

strict.doc: Decodes with the inner decoder, and when the input is an object gives unknown_field for every member whose name is not among the known names and that the inner decoder has not already reported unknown, in the order of the input's members, after the inner decoder's issues. A member is reported once, by the innermost strict that does not know it, and nested strict forms accept only members every one of them knows. The inner decoder's result is discarded when there is any unknown member.

nullable.doc: Gives null for a JSON null, and decodes anything else, an absent value included, with the inner decoder.

enum.doc: Decodes a string with the string decoder and gives the symbol whose name equals it under ASCII case folding. Otherwise gives invalid_format.enum with allowed listing the ASCII-lower-cased names in code point order.

literal.doc: Decodes a string with the string decoder and accepts it when it equals the literal; otherwise gives invalid_format.literal.

discriminate.doc: Reads the tag, the member the tag field names, with the string decoder, and decodes the whole input with the variant the tag names. At the tag field's path, a non-object input gives type_mismatch (expected "object"), and a missing, null or non-string tag gives what the string decoder gives for it: required, or type_mismatch (expected "string"). A tag that names no variant gives not_allowed at the tag field's path, with allowed listing the variant names in code point order and no actual.

discriminateBy.doc: As discriminate, except that the tag is what the tag decoder gives for the whole input; the tag decoder's issues are given as they are. A tag that names no variant gives not_allowed at the tag field's path, as discriminate does.

oneOf.doc: Tries each candidate in order on the same input and gives the first success. When all fail, gives one_of_failed at the input's path, whose candidates list, for each candidate by index, the issues it gave, each with its path, code, message and meta.

withDefault.doc: Gives the default for a JSON null or an absent value, and decodes anything else with the inner decoder.

recover.doc: Decodes with the inner decoder, and gives the fallback instead of any failure.

recoverWith.doc: Decodes with the inner decoder, and gives what the fixture computes from the issues instead of any failure.

field.doc: A required field: decodes the member of that name with the decoder, at the member's path. An absent member is passed to the decoder as absent. When the input is not an object, gives type_mismatch (expected "object") at the member's path instead.

optionalField.doc: An optional field: gives empty when the member is absent or the input is not an object, and otherwise decodes the member with the decoder.

optionalNullableField.doc: Gives absent when the member is absent or the input is not an object, null when the member is JSON null, and otherwise the value the decoder gives, as present.

flat.doc: Decodes the whole input, not a member of it, with the decoder, and contributes the decoder's value as one element of the product; the decoder's issues appear at the position of the flat field.

operations.name: trim
operations.doc: Removes leading and trailing characters with the Unicode White_Space property (Unicode 18.0.0).

operations.name: toLowerCase
operations.doc: Lower-cases with the Unicode 18.0.0 default lowercase mapping: the full mappings of UnicodeData.txt and SpecialCasing.txt, including their context-dependent ones (a capital sigma becomes a final sigma where the Final_Sigma condition holds), and no language-specific tailoring.

operations.name: toUpperCase
operations.doc: Upper-cases with the Unicode 18.0.0 default uppercase mapping: the full mappings of UnicodeData.txt and SpecialCasing.txt (ß becomes SS), and no language-specific tailoring.

operations.name: normalize
operations.doc: Applies Unicode 18.0.0 normalization in the form given, NFC if none.

operations.name: nonBlank
operations.doc: Gives blank for a string that is empty or holds only characters with the Unicode White_Space property (Unicode 18.0.0).

operations.name: minLength
operations.doc: Gives too_short when the string has fewer Unicode code points than min.

operations.name: maxLength
operations.doc: Gives too_long when the string has more Unicode code points than max.

operations.name: fixedLength
operations.doc: Gives invalid_length when the string does not have exactly that many Unicode code points.

operations.name: oneOf
operations.doc: Gives not_allowed, with allowed in code point order, when the string is none of the allowed ones. The allowed strings are distinct.

operations.name: startsWith
operations.doc: Requires the prefix.

operations.name: endsWith
operations.doc: Requires the suffix.

operations.name: includes
operations.doc: Requires the substring.

operations.name: pattern
operations.doc: Gives invalid_format, with the pattern as written, unless the whole string is one of the strings the pattern denotes. The pattern is written in the pattern language of spec/pattern.md, which says what it means and which patterns are admitted: its matching is over Unicode scalar values, case-sensitive, and of the whole string, and a pattern that writes a count above 134217727, nests groups more than 200 deep or comes to more than 250000 states is not an argument.

operations.name: email
operations.doc: Gives invalid_format.email unless the string is in an ASCII lexical profile of RFC 5321's Mailbox: Dot-string "@" Domain. The local part is one or more atoms of RFC 5322 atext (A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and !#$%&'*+-/=?^_`{|}~) joined by single dots, of at most 64 octets; the domain is one or more labels joined by single dots, each a letter or digit, optionally followed by letters, digits and hyphens ending in a letter or digit, of at most 63 octets (RFC 1035), the domain at most 255 octets; the whole mailbox is at most 254 octets, since RFC 5321 limits a path, which encloses the mailbox in < and >, to 256 (as verified erratum 1690 to RFC 3696 also derives). A quoted local part, an address literal and SMTPUTF8 are outside the profile. Only the syntax is checked: a single-label or all-digit domain (a@localhost, a@123) is accepted, and whether the domain resolves or can be used in an SMTP transaction is not checked.

operations.name: ipv4
operations.doc: Gives invalid_format.ipv4 unless the string is an IPv4 address as RFC 3986 writes IPv4address: four decimal numbers from 0 to 255 in ASCII digits, separated by ., with no leading zero.

operations.name: ipv6
operations.doc: Gives invalid_format.ipv6 unless the string is an IPv6 address as RFC 3986 writes IPv6address (the text form of RFC 4291 section 2.2): eight groups of one to four hexadecimal digits in either case, at most one :: standing for one or more zero groups, and optionally an IPv4 address as ipv4 accepts it in place of the last two groups. Brackets are rejected. The address may be followed by % and a zone ID, any non-empty text without % or U+0000, only when it is link-local unicast (fe80::/10) or multicast whose scope field is 1 to D.

operations.name: ip
operations.doc: Gives invalid_format.ip unless the string is what ipv4 or ipv6 accepts.

operations.name: ulid
operations.doc: Gives invalid_format.ulid unless the string is a ULID in its canonical text form: 26 characters of Crockford's base 32 (0-9 and the letters but I, L, O and U), in either case, whose value is at most 7ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ (128 bits). The string is given unchanged.

operations.name: cuid
operations.doc: Gives invalid_format.cuid unless the string is a CUID of version 1: c followed by 24 lower-case ASCII letters or digits, 25 characters in all. A CUID2 is not one.

operations.name: uuid
operations.doc: Reads 32 hexadecimal digits in either case, grouped 8-4-4-4-12 by hyphens (RFC 9562 section 4), of any version and variant, the nil and max UUIDs included. Braces, a urn:uuid: prefix, missing hyphens and shortened groups give invalid_format.uuid.

operations.name: url
operations.doc: Reads an RFC 3986 URI, as uri reads it, that meets the http and https scheme requirements of RFC 9110 section 4.2: its scheme is http or https, compared ASCII case-insensitively, and it has an authority with a non-empty host; anything else gives invalid_format.url. The host is RFC 3986's, not a DNS name, and the port is not checked against a range.

operations.name: uri
operations.doc: Reads a URI as the URI production of RFC 3986 section 3 derives it: a scheme, a colon, the hierarchical part, an optional query and an optional fragment, in ASCII with every other character percent-encoded. The value is the string as written. Everything the grammar derives is accepted, an empty path (a:), an empty authority or host (a://, http://), an IPvFuture host and a port of any length included; a scheme-specific rule, such as http's non-empty host, is not checked. A relative reference, and anything else the grammar does not derive, gives invalid_format.uri, as does an IPv6 host with a zone identifier, which RFC 9844 removed from the URI syntax again.

operations.name: toInt
operations.doc: Reads an optional sign (+ or -) followed by one or more ASCII digits, leading zeros allowed, with nothing else. Anything else gives type_mismatch with expected "integer"; an integer outside int32 gives type_mismatch.numeric_range. A message, when given, is the message of either issue.

operations.name: toLong
operations.doc: As toInt, for int64, with expected "long".

operations.name: toDecimal
operations.doc: Reads a decimal number matching [+-]?([0-9]+(\.[0-9]*)?|\.[0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?, keeping the scale it is written with; anything else, and an exponent the scale cannot hold, gives type_mismatch with expected "decimal".

operations.name: toBool
operations.doc: Reads true, 1, yes or on as true and false, 0, no or off as false, ASCII case-insensitively; anything else gives type_mismatch with expected "boolean".

operations.name: iso8601
operations.doc: Reads an instant: a date as date reads it, with the years of the instant range; an upper-case T; hh:mm:ss, the seconds required, optionally followed by . and 1 to 9 digits; and an offset, upper-case Z, or + or - with hh:mm or hh:mm:ss of at most 18 hours. The offset is applied. 24:00:00 with no fraction is the start of the next day, and hour 24 with a fraction gives invalid_format.instant, all-zero or not; a second 60 is rejected at any offset. Anything else, and a moment outside the instant range, gives invalid_format.instant.

operations.name: date
operations.doc: Reads year-mm-dd in ASCII digits: a year of four digits from 0000 to 9999, or a sign and five or more digits with no leading zero, or - and four digits other than 0000, from -999999999 to 999999999; the date must exist in the proleptic Gregorian calendar. Anything else gives invalid_format.date.

operations.name: time
operations.doc: Reads hh:mm, hh:mm:ss, or hh:mm:ss followed by . and 1 to 9 digits, in ASCII digits, with hours from 00 to 23 and minutes and seconds from 00 to 59. 24:00, a second 60 and an offset give invalid_format.time.

operations.name: dateTime
operations.doc: Reads a date as date reads it, an upper-case T, and a time as time reads it; anything else gives invalid_format.date_time.

operations.name: offsetDateTime
operations.doc: Reads a date-time as dateTime reads it followed by an offset: upper-case Z, or + or - with hh:mm or hh:mm:ss of at most 18 hours, minutes and seconds at most 59. +00:00 and -00:00 are the zero offset, the same value as Z; RFC 9557 gives -00:00 the meaning of Z and +00:00 another, which the value does not keep. The offset is kept, not applied. Anything else gives invalid_format.offset_date_time.

operations.name: min
operations.doc: Gives out_of_range.minimum when the value is less than min. Floats are compared in the float order of the value model (-0 is less than +0); decimals by value.

operations.name: max
operations.doc: Gives out_of_range.maximum when the value is greater than max, compared as min compares.

operations.name: range
operations.doc: Gives out_of_range.range when the value is outside [min, max], compared as min compares.

operations.name: positive
operations.doc: Gives out_of_range.positive unless the value is greater than zero, compared as min compares. min is the least value allowed for an integer (1), and zero otherwise.

operations.name: negative
operations.doc: Gives out_of_range.negative unless the value is less than zero, compared as min compares; -0 is less than +0 and so negative. max is the greatest value allowed for an integer (-1), and zero otherwise.

operations.name: nonNegative
operations.doc: Gives out_of_range.non_negative, with min zero, when the value is less than zero, compared as min compares; -0 is less than +0.

operations.name: nonPositive
operations.doc: Gives out_of_range.non_positive, with max zero, when the value is greater than zero, compared as min compares.

operations.name: oneOf
operations.doc: Gives not_allowed, with allowed in ascending order, when the value is none of the allowed ones, compared as the value model compares them (for floats, +0 and -0 differ, and NaN is NaN). The allowed values are distinct as the value model compares them.

operations.name: multipleOf
operations.doc: Gives not_multiple_of when the value is not a multiple of the divisor.

operations.name: scale
operations.doc: Gives invalid_scale when the decimal's scale is greater than max.

operations.name: isTrue
operations.doc: Gives invalid_value, with expected true, for false.

operations.name: nonempty
operations.doc: Gives too_small.nonempty, with min 1, when there is no element.

operations.name: minSize
operations.doc: Gives too_small when there are fewer than min elements.

operations.name: maxSize
operations.doc: Gives too_big when there are more than max elements.

operations.name: fixedSize
operations.doc: Gives invalid_size unless there are exactly that many elements.

operations.name: unique
operations.doc: Gives duplicate_element when an element occurs more than once, compared as the value model compares them; duplicates lists each such element once, ordered by the position of the occurrence that first makes it a duplicate, its second occurrence: [1,2,2,1] lists 2, a duplicate from position 2, before 1, a duplicate from position 3.

operations.name: contains
operations.doc: Gives missing_element unless the element occurs, compared as the value model compares them.

operations.name: containsAll
operations.doc: Gives missing_elements unless every element occurs, compared as the value model compares them; missing lists, in the order given, each given element that does not occur, as many times as it was given.

operations.name: toSet
operations.doc: Gives the set of the elements.

operations.name: before
operations.doc: Gives out_of_range.before unless the value is strictly before the bound. Offset date-times are compared chronologically, by instant alone, so 09:00Z is not before 10:00+01:00, the same instant.

operations.name: after
operations.doc: Gives out_of_range.after unless the value is strictly after the bound, compared as before compares.

operations.name: between
operations.doc: Gives out_of_range.between unless from <= value <= to, compared as before compares.

operations.name: map
operations.doc: Gives what the fixture computes from the value.

operations.name: refine
operations.doc: Gives the issue the fixture declares, at the decoder's path, when the fixture's predicate does not hold.

operations.name: flatMap
operations.doc: Gives what the fixture computes, or the issue it declares, whose path is relative to the decoder's path.

string.doc: Encodes a string as a JSON string.

object.doc: Encodes the value as a JSON object with one member per property, in declaration order. No two properties write the same member.

propertyWithDefault.doc: The member name, whose value is what the encoder gives for the getter's result, or for the default when the getter gives null.
